# ADR 0001: One secured Spring Boot service (modular monolith) with an external identity provider

← [Architecture](../README.md) · [Capstone brief](../../README.md)

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Capstone:** Fraud case management service

## Context

Fraud case management service has closely related capabilities and one team. Authentication is a solved problem that should not be reimplemented, and the service must work with any OAuth2/OIDC provider.

## Decision

Build one Spring Boot 4 service, packaged by feature, owning one PostgreSQL database. It is an OAuth2 resource server: Keycloak (or a managed provider) issues JWTs; the service validates signature, issuer, audience and expiry locally using the provider's cached public keys, and authorises with scopes, roles and ownership checks.

## Consequences

No passwords or sessions in the service; any compliant identity provider can be swapped in by changing the issuer URI. Token revocation is only as fast as the token lifetime (keep access tokens short, 5 minutes here).

## Alternatives considered

Session cookies with a login form in the service (couples identity to one app); opaque tokens with introspection (a network call per request); microservices per capability (Phase 3).
